chunks.arabic_text: الرَّبِيعُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ عُمَرَ، الْكُوفِيُّ. رَوَى عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَبِي زِيَادٍ السَّكُونِيِّ "كِتَابَهُ"، عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān ibn ʿUmar, the Kufan. Narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād al-Sakūnī his book, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad (peace be upon him).

chunks.arabic_text: أَمَرُهُ قَرِيبٌ، قَدْ طُعِنَ عَلَيْهِ، وَيَجُوزُ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ شَاهِدًا.

translations.en: His affair is near (acceptable), he has been calumniated (criticized), and it is permissible for him to be brought out as a witness.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* evaluates al-Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān al-Kufī, a narrator of Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (AS), whose reliability is deemed sufficient ('qarīb') despite specific criticisms ('ṭunna ʿalayh'). The scholar concludes that his testimony is legally permissible ('yujāzu an yukhraja shāhidan'), illustrating the nuanced Shia methodology of accepting narrators with minor flaws for evidentiary purposes.
en.seo_question: What is the biographical status of Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān al-Kufī in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.طُعِنَ عَلَيْهِ: He was calumniated/criticized (technical term for narrator criticism)
